module_title: Primary Memory - Technical Classifications of RAM/ROM and Cache Memory
introduction: This intermediate tier targets the technical sub-types of RAM (SRAM vs. DRAM) and ROM (PROM, EPROM, EEPROM), which are heavily tested in SSC CGL Tier-1 and Banking Prelims. We also introduce Cache memory, the ultimate speed booster.

core_concepts.title: Types of RAM: SRAM vs. DRAM
core_concepts.description:
- DRAM (Dynamic RAM): Cheaper and slower. It must be constantly 'refreshed' thousands of times per second to retain data. Your computer's main RAM sticks (like DDR4) are DRAM.
- SRAM (Static RAM): Expensive and extremely fast. It does NOT need to be refreshed. Because of its speed, it is primarily used to build 'Cache Memory'.

core_concepts.title: Types of ROM (PROM, EPROM, EEPROM)
core_concepts.description:
- PROM (Programmable ROM): Can be programmed only once by the user. 
- EPROM (Erasable PROM): Data can be erased by exposing the chip to strong Ultraviolet (UV) rays.
- EEPROM (Electrically Erasable PROM): Data can be erased and rewritten electrically without removing the chip. Modern Flash memory uses this technology.

core_concepts.title: Cache Memory
core_concepts.description: An ultra-fast buffer memory physically located between the CPU and the main RAM. It temporarily stores the most frequently used data and instructions so the CPU doesn't have to wait for the slower RAM, drastically speeding up processing.

important_entities.name: Flash Memory
important_entities.significance: Your Pen Drives, SD Cards, and SSDs are all practical applications of EEPROM (Flash Memory). They are non-volatile storage mediums that can be electrically rewritten.

important_entities.name: Refresh Circuit
important_entities.significance: Because DRAM is built using tiny capacitors that leak electrical charge, it requires a dedicated 'refresh circuit' to periodically rewrite the data, making it slower than SRAM.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Is a Pen Drive RAM or ROM?
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Because you can quickly write and delete files on a Pen Drive, students assume it functions like RAM. False! A Pen Drive retains data without power, meaning it is a Non-Volatile storage device based on EEPROM (a type of ROM) technology.
Statement-based questions often ask where Cache is located. It is always stationed 'between the CPU and the Main Memory (RAM)', NEVER between the RAM and the Hard Disk.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: E needs UV, EE needs Electricity
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: EPROM has one 'E', erased by UV light. EEPROM has a double 'E', erased Electrically.

exam_strategy_tips: Examiners love testing the difference between SRAM and DRAM. Always pair 'Dynamic' with the need for 'Refreshing', and 'Static' with 'No Refreshing'.
